clue.text: Bitter with pen under tree

indicators.note: in a down clue the pen's letters sit below the tree's letters

parts.note: the acer is the maple genus of trees
a Bic is a familiar brand of ballpoint pen

explanation.surface: Someone sour-tempered sits writing beneath a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: An acerbic remark is sharp and sour, so the word is a synonym for bitter in tone.

clue.text: Having 13 loyalty three times covers two turns

annotationWithheld.why: Having 13 loyalty three times covers two turns: TREBLE takes one U after TR and another after TREBL, two separate insertions both driven by the single word 'covers', which the grammar cannot express without that indicator doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Having 13 loyalty three times covers two turns

clue.text: See 15
See 15
Diverting 24 that 12 3 4

indicators.note: diverting sends the letters off on a new route, so the scholar's word is rearranged

parts.note: 24 across is SAVANT, the scholar

explanation.surface: A rearranged scholar is the thing that will get you anywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 12 3 4 is WILL GET YOU ANYWHERE, so the definition is 'that will get you anywhere'; 'Diverting' rearranges SAVANT, the answer to 24, into the gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: A satellite navigation system in a car guides the driver to any destination, so it will take you anywhere.

clue.text: I receive signal with an audible note

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: audible means the words are taken as heard, not as spelt

parts.note: a tenner is a ten-pound banknote; heard aloud it gives the ending of the aerial's name

explanation.surface: A radio aerial describes itself, with a hint of a musical note.
explanation.walkthrough: A TENNER is British slang for a ten-pound note; said with AN in front it sounds like the aerial. 'note' looks musical but is money.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerial is the device that picks up broadcast signals, so it can say it receives signals.

clue.text: 12 linked with 22 is far from 2

definitions.meaning: Will (12) gives Will ..., a Merry Man of Robin Hood linked with Friar Tuck (22)
red is the colour furthest from true blue, the colour of conservatives

explanation.walkthrough: Will Scarlet and Friar Tuck are both companions of Robin Hood; politically, red stands for the left, opposite to the true-blue Tories.
explanation.definitionFit: Will Scarlet is the outlaw companion beside Friar Tuck, and the bright red colour contrasts sharply with blue.

clue.text: Murdered king guillotined at US city, which is weird

indicators.note: a guillotine takes off the head, so the first letter of the king's name goes

parts.note: Duncan is the king murdered in Shakespeare's Macbeth
NY is the abbreviation for New York

explanation.surface: A beheaded king in an American city makes for something strange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guillotined' removes the D from DUNCAN, leaving UNCAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncanny means strangely unsettling or beyond explanation, a close synonym for weird.

clue.text: Probability with goals of all-sorts

parts.note: odds express the probability of an outcome
and means together with
ends are aims or goals

explanation.surface: Chances and aims combine into a jumble of everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Odds and ends are miscellaneous leftover items, an assortment much like all-sorts.

clue.text: Journalist in colour wanting too much

indicators.note: in places the journalist inside the colour's letters

parts.note: grey is a colour
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A drab-looking reporter is grasping for more.
explanation.definitionFit: Being greedy means desiring more than one needs, which is wanting too much.

clue.text: Maxim of Du Maurier "Drops get put into ground"

parts.note: dew forms as drops of moisture
to inter is to bury, putting into the ground

explanation.surface: A saying attributed to the novelist about drops sinking into the earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maxim' looks like a saying, but it is Maxim de Winter, hero of Daphne du Maurier's novel Rebecca.
explanation.definitionFit: Maxim de Winter is the brooding widower of Manderley in Daphne du Maurier's novel Rebecca.

clue.text: See 15
University state, fifth in Ireland, good and straightforward

parts.note: NSW is New South Wales, an Australian state

indicators.note: in puts the fifth inside the name for Ireland

parts.note: Erin is a poetic name for Ireland
V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: A university, a state, Ireland and goodness all lined up plainly.
explanation.definitionFit: Unswerving means not deviating from a course, hence direct and straightforward.

clue.text: Page among groups that are well camouflaged

parts.note: a leaf is a page of a book
in means among
sects are religious groups

explanation.surface: A page tucked among various factions hides itself well.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaf insects are tropical creatures shaped and coloured like leaves, famed examples of camouflage.

clue.text: Tyre problem — the same by Shakespeare (I'm amazed at your boast!) when year off — brings humorous acceptance of sweet talk

annotationWithheld.why: Tyre problem — the same by Shakespeare ...: 'Tyre problem' must give FLAT and, via 'the same', the anagram TERY too, so 'Tyre' does two jobs (the blog's commenters note the same liberty)
annotationWithheld.clue: Tyre problem — the same by Shakespeare (I'm amazed at your boast!) when year off — brings humorous acceptance of sweet talk

clue.text: Garnish bird on which quartet dined

parts.note: a tit is a small bird
IV is the Roman numeral for four
ate means dined

explanation.surface: A small bird provides the meal on which four diners feasted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on which' sets the quartet and the meal after the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: To titivate is to smarten up or adorn, much as to garnish is to decorate.

clue.text: Bird seems to miss catching possible prey

indicators.note: catching means holding the prey inside the word for missing

parts.note: to fail is to miss
an ant is something a bird might eat

explanation.surface: A bird seems to fail to catch what it hunts.
explanation.definitionFit: A fantail is a bird, either a fan-tailed pigeon or a flycatcher of Asia and Australasia.

clue.text: Flower poisonous if a traffic controller swallows it

indicators.note: swallows means the cone takes the next word inside itself

parts.note: a traffic cone controls the flow of vehicles
taken as written

explanation.surface: A poisonous bloom could be fatal if swallowed by someone directing traffic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'traffic controller' suggests a person, but it is a plastic road cone.
explanation.definitionFit: Aconite, or monkshood, is a flowering plant whose roots and leaves are highly toxic.

clue.text: I can take picture, book, play, or picture

definitions.meaning: a camera speaking of itself, as something that takes photographs
the title of John van Druten's stage play and the 1955 film, from Isherwood's Berlin stories

explanation.walkthrough: 'picture' first means a photograph, then a film.
explanation.definitionFit: The play and film took their title from Isherwood's line 'I am a camera with its shutter open'.

clue.text: French city from which it went after a queen

definitions.text: French city from which it went after a queen

indicators.note: after places the remains of the town word behind the queen

parts.note: Anne was a queen of England

indicators.note: went means the word it has departed from the town word

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A French town loses something after a queen's arrival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'went' removes a two-letter pronoun from the town word. Annecy is a French town; the whole clue defines it because 'city' also serves in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Annecy is a lakeside town in the Haute-Savoie region of south-east France.

clue.text: Fool both of us? Suppose

parts.note: an ass is a fool
you and me, written as U for you plus ME

explanation.surface: Someone calls the pair of us idiots and supposes it is true.
explanation.walkthrough: U is text-speak for 'you'; with ME it makes the two of us.
explanation.definitionFit: To assume is to take something as true without proof, which is to suppose.

clue.text: Folded food?

definitions.meaning: a fold sewn into fabric; folded describes cloth with such a fold
British schoolboy slang for food, especially sweets and snacks

explanation.walkthrough: TUCK is old British school slang for snacks, as in a tuck shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A tuck is a stitched fold in cloth, and tuck is also schoolboy slang for snacks.

annotationWithheld.clue: Second instant with boy at airport

clue.text: Scholar had a chair where leaders entered

indicators.note: entered means the leaders go inside the word for sitting

parts.note: to have a chair is to have sat down
the van is the leading part of an army, so leaders are the van

explanation.surface: An academic sat in a chair where the front-runners came in.
explanation.definitionFit: A savant is a learned person, a scholar of deep knowledge.

clue.text: What's wrong with wax being 2?

parts.note: a sin is something wrong
cere is a wax-like substance

explanation.surface: Asking what harm wax does by being loyal.
explanation.walkthrough: 2 is TRUE BLUE, here in the sense of genuine and true.
explanation.definitionFit: True blue can mean genuine and honest, so someone sincere is true to their word.

clue.text: I am first with pictures to be 25 in 15

parts.note: I'm is the contraction of I am
I is the Roman numeral one, as in a monarch's first
the Tate is the London art gallery full of pictures

explanation.surface: I claim first place with my artworks to show genuine admiration.
explanation.walkthrough: 25 is SINCERE and 15 is FLATTERY: imitation is the sincerest form of flattery. The TATE is a London art gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says imitation is the sincerest form of flattery, so to copy is to be sincere in flattering.
